thread:
alex: Heads-up — thinking about adding a per-route 'version pin' toggle in the console so tenants can force requests to v1 or v2 during migrations. Main goal: a single-click safe mode for customers to stop silent switches. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
jin: Love the idea. Two quick worries: quota accounting (if we pin to v1 but billing expects v2 tokens) and telemetry signals getting fragmented.
pat: Agreed. Also need to decide if pin is soft (console hint + sampling) or hard (control-plane routing rule). Hard pin is simpler for customers but more infra risk.
sam: If we go hard, we should expose an escape hatch API. Something like POST /internal/routes/{route}/unpin with audit log. ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: routing-service v3 (will include pin rule matcher) — ETA tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
lee: UX note: show expected delta in per-token cost and latency before they confirm pin. Small modal: "Pin to v1 — expected +12% latency, -8% unit cost". We can compute using model profiles.
alex: Good call on modal copy. For infra: my preference is soft default (console toggles a policy that prefers the pinned version with sticky affinity) and an admin-only hard pin. That keeps rollout flexibility.
jin: Telemetry plan: emit an event: compat.pin.changed with fields (route, from_version, to_version, actor) and also increment metric compat.pin.active{version=v1|v2}. Sampling: record a tiny trace for first 1000 requests after pin to catch regressions.
pat: About quota: we need to ensure tokens are attributed to the version actually executed. I propose we add a header passthrough: "X-Redwood-Effective-Version" set by the router, and billing reads that. Minimal change to billing service.
sam: Caveat: some SDKs strip unknown headers. We should also write the effective version to the request metadata in the proxy span so any downstream baggage can get it.
lee: Console UX: add a diff view that shows which routes will be impacted and a quick sampling link to preview 1k requests (shadowing) before pin. Button copy: "Preview pin (shadow 1k)".
alex: Rollout mechanics: allow pin to be time-limited (TTL) e.g., 24h default, with auto-unpin. Helps avoid forgotten pins. Also an org-level override with audit.
jin: Implementation sketch: routing-service keeps a Pin table: (org_id, route_id, target_version, mode=[soft|hard], expires_at). Router checks Pin table first. For soft mode, it emits a && fallback behavior: if target not available, keep existing fallback.
pat: Performance: Pin table reads must be cheap — cache in local ring and invalidate on change. Invalidation storm is a risk if many tenants pin concurrently; need backoff.
sam: Telemetry question: do we track "pin flips" as an SLO event? e.g., when pin causes an increase in 5xx or latency we auto-notify the tenant via console.
lee: We should surface a small alert card: "We detected a 3% p50 latency increase after pin — would you like to rollback?" with quick rollback button.
alex: Agreed. For guardrails: forbid hard pin to versions that are EOL in <30 days. Prevent customers pinning to deprecated variants.
jin: Edge cases: streaming endpoints (server-sent tokens) need to preserve KV cache compatibility. If v2 uses different KV layout, pinning to v1 must ensure cache keying remains consistent. Add a migration hook to check seqlen and kv-schema.
pat: Also need to update canary/experiment framework: pinned routes should be excluded from automatic version promotions.
sam: Ops ask: Add an audit log entry and a rate-limited slack notification to #incidents or #customer-impact when a hard pin is applied. That helps SRE triage.
lee: Copy for modal: short, clear: "Pinning locks route to X version. Use for urgent behaviour stability. Can increase cost or latency. Preview before applying."
alex: Next steps: 1) jin + pat make infra PR for Pin table + header propagation; 2) sam add telemetry events and console alert hooks; 3) lee mock the modal and diff UI. ops-bot: I created a tracking ticket: RW-13521 — routing pin feature.
jin: One more thought — allow a 'soft pin ratio' (e.g., 95% pinned, 5% probes to new version). That would let us detect regressions while maintaining stability.
pat: Nice. We'll need new metrics: routing.pin.pct and routing.pin.probe_errors. And quota split rules when probe hits different token counts.
sam: Okay team — I'll sketch the SLO checks that can trigger auto-unpin. Let's sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. :calendar: 
alex: Thanks — appreciate the quick inputs.
